question: Who will be the largest Republican donor in the 2026 cycle, as of Election Day?

calls.reasoning: Musk has given ~$369M this cycle (WaPo Oct 12; CNBC Oct 15-16), including $158M to Senate Leadership Fund in Q3 and $89M to America PAC, making him the largest known midterm donor. The nearest Republican rivals (Uihlein, Yass, Adelson, Andreessen/Horowitz) are historically in the tens of millions to ~$100M. With ~13 days left and lagging FEC filings, a rank change is very unlikely. Remaining risk is leaderboard labeling/aggregation quirks. No human prediction market found for this question.
calls.dossier:
- WaPo (2026-10-12): Elon Musk 'quietly becomes biggest known donor in midterm contests'; ~$369M of his own money this cycle, mostly to GOP-aligned groups (SLF top donation $168M cumulative; also America PAC, CLF, Fight for Kentucky, Lone Star Liberty PAC >$10M each).
- CNBC (2026-10-15): Musk gave $158M to Senate Leadership Fund in Sept 2026 (two checks, $75M and $83M); 58% of SLF's record $272.9M Q3.
- CNBC (2026-10-16): Musk put >$276M into federal political groups in Q3 2026, incl. $89M to America PAC.
- The Hill: Musk gave nearly $160M to a Texas PAC backing Paxton.
- WaPo leaderboard: the top 50 donors total ~$2.39B; dominated by Republicans. Largest Democratic: Soros family ~$102.8M.
- Background: Winklevoss brothers gave $10M in August; Uihlein, Yass, Adelson and Andreessen/Horowitz are historically large GOP donors, but no 2026 figures were found near Musk's.
- Status quo: Musk holds the top spot.
- Resolves off the WaPo Top 50 leaderboard as displayed on Nov 3, 2026, not off FEC totals directly; the leaderboard lags FEC filings.
- Event window: snapshot on 2026-11-03; as of 2026-10-21 about 13 days remain.
- Searched but not found: current exact amounts for Uihlein, Yass, Adelson and Andreessen/Horowitz (leaderboard page returned 403); any prediction market on this question.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the top Republican donor in a WaPo/FEC leaderboard about two weeks before the election almost never changes, because the gaps are in the hundreds of millions and only one or two FEC reports remain. The Washington Post (Oct 12 and Oct 21, 2026) reports Musk is the biggest known donor in the midterms at about $369M, with $168M to SLF, $139M to America PAC and $30M to CLF. In late August, Andreessen & Horowitz led at $115M, Yass had $93.8M and the Uihleins about $70M. Musk's lead of more than $250M can't realistically be closed by Nov 3. The main risks are how the leaderboard groups or displays donors (for example, if Musk's giving through entities is shown differently or the page isn't updated with Q3 data) and how 'Republican-aligned' gets interpreted. No human prediction market was found: the Manifold candidates the harness surfaced are unrelated contracts.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree, citing WaPo Oct 12 and CNBC/Hankyoreh, that Musk leads at ~$369M. The disputes are factual details that cannot change the top spot. The size of the America PAC component ($76M, $89M or $139M) does not matter, because every run reports the same ~$369M total. Who is second (Uihleins at ~$138M in an October summary vs Andreessen/Horowitz at $115M in August data) also does not matter, since both trail by more than $200M. The newer October figure probably reflects the current leaderboard. The one judgment dispute is how much weight to put on leaderboard grouping or labeling risk. I put about 4-5% on non-Musk outcomes combined. Musk's giving is overwhelmingly to GOP groups, so a 'Republican-aligned' label is near-certain. I carry forward Run 3's reference class.
